text:
mike_support: escalated from customer — when using structured output mode the response stream sometimes yields unparsable JSON if the input contains control/formatting glyphs (RTL marks, vertical tabs). customer sees final error `parse_error: invalid JSON` and a 502.

olga_support: can you paste a minimal repro and the request_id?

mike_support: request_id: req_20260317_9a2b. minimal repro (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"mode":"structured","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"bio":{"type":"string"}}},"input":"Hello\u202Eworld\u000B!"}'
```
Response (captured stream chunks):
```json
{"chunk":1,"data":"{\"bio\":\"Hello\u202Eworld"}
{"chunk":2,"data":"\u000B!\"}"}
```
Then assembly fails with `JSONDecodeError: Unexpected control character at position 42`.

nina_engineer: :eyes: thanks — this looks like unescaped literal control chars crossing chunk boundaries. our JSON-mode assembler expects every string to be valid JSON in-flight; if a chunk boundary splits an escaped sequence or injects a raw control glyph (e.g. U+000B vertical tab, U+202E RLO) the concatenated stream becomes invalid. what model and replica was this on?

mike_support: customer on dedicated pool `ded-phi-2`, model `open-llama-70b` (quantized). provided raw chunks above from their capture.

nina_engineer: i can reproduce locally by sending a string with U+000B inside the prompt while streaming with ~64 token chunking. quick notes:
- streaming write can split a `\\uXXXX` escape across chunks if the runtime emits the literal bytes for the control glyph instead of the escape sequence.
- our assembler currently assumes chunk data is valid JSON text and performs a simple concat + parse; it does not re-escape control codepoints.

short-term mitigation suggestions:
- sanitize client-side: replace control-range chars before send: `s/([\u0000-\u001F\u007F-\u009F\u202A-\u202E])/\\\\u{hex}/g` or strip them.
- alternative: base64-encode user-provided free-text fields and decode in postprocess, prevents JSON-mode assembler from seeing raw control glyphs.
- internal toggle: enable `string_safety: "escape_control_chars"` (internal flag) in request to force the generator to emit `\\\\uXXXX` escapes for control points.

nina_engineer: filing ENG-3317 to track a proper fix (make assembler resilient to literal control chars + ensure the runtime always emits safe escapes when structured mode is requested). adding repro steps and a unit test.

ci-bot: created ticket ENG-3317 and attached reproduction logs (link: https://internal.redwood/ENG-3317).

olga_support: copying workaround to the customer, advising short-term sanitize or base64 trick. escalating priority to P1 for Dedicated customer SLA. :thumbsup:

mike_support: thanks — customer notified, they've applied client-side sanitize as a temporary workaround. will update when they confirm stability.
